context: Scrollytelling bar chart of global temperature anomalies (1884–2023) with 5 progressive narrative steps: baseline band, volcanic events, color-coded bars, moving average, and regression with per-decade inset.
first_impression: Clean and controlled — the sticky single-chart layout with one narrative step visible at a time keeps cognitive load low throughout most of the scroll journey.
what_works: Progressive disclosure is well-paced: each step adds exactly one visual layer (color, moving average, regression) so the viewer is never asked to process more than one new encoding at once. The two-color palette (warm red / cool blue) is semantically loaded and perceptually unambiguous, making the post-1970 shift immediately legible.
what_doesnt: Step 4 breaks the one-idea-per-step discipline by simultaneously showing colored bars, the moving average, a regression line, a slope annotation box, a per-decade inset mini bar chart, and a 2023 callout — roughly 6 concurrent elements competing for attention. The rotated y-axis label is clipped at the left viewport edge in the screenshot, making the axis unit hard to read without already knowing what the chart shows.
